constraints:
• 2 <= users.length <= 10^4, and user names are distinct.
  • 0 <= logs.length <= 10^5
  • Each log entry has the format "timestamp userA userB" with 0 <= timestamp <= 10^9, and both users appear in users.
  • Logs may be given out of timestamp order.
why: Process edges in sorted order: sort the ride logs by timestamp and union the two riders of each. Keep a component count that drops on every real merge; the timestamp at which it reaches 1 is the answer.
hints: Connections only ever join groups, never split them. What order should you replay the logs in?
Sort by timestamp and union-find the users. How do you know, without scanning everyone, that all users are in one group?
Start with components = len(users); every union that merges two different roots decrements it; return the timestamp when it hits 1, else -1. O(L log L).
pitfalls: Logs arrive out of order; sorting first is required.
Parse the timestamp as an integer, not a string ("10" < "5" as strings).
